notes: Russian MoD-controlled successor to Wagner in Africa

label: Akhmat forces
notes: 'Ахмат' is also a personal name and a football club

notes: Russian MoD penal assault companies formed from convicts

notes: successor MoD convict recruitment program; confidence medium on usage frequency

label: Española volunteer unit
notes: football-ultras volunteer unit; Ukrainian spelling varies

label: Somali Battalion
notes: DPR unit (Givi); bare 'Сомали' also = the country

label: Russian Airborne Forces (VDV)
notes: 3-letter acronym kept deliberately; match as whole word

label: FSB
notes: 3-letter acronym kept deliberately; match as whole word

notes: Rusich co-founder, callsign 'Slavyan'; 'Петровский' is also a common surname and district name

label: Andrei Troshev
notes: Wagner executive, callsign 'Седой' (not included: generic word)

label: Andrei Belousov
notes: Russian defence minister from 2024; common surname

label: Leonid Pasechnik

label: Armed Forces of Ukraine
notes: 3-letter acronyms kept deliberately; match as whole word

label: 'Baba Yaga' heavy bomber drone
notes: Russian nickname for Ukrainian heavy multicopter bombers

label: 'Chmobik' (mobilized soldier, derogatory)

label: 'Kyiv regime' / 'junta'
notes: Russian propaganda term for the Ukrainian government

label: 'Khokhly' (slur for Ukrainians)

label: 'Natsiki' / 'natsbaty' (Nazis — propaganda)
notes: Russian propaganda label for Ukrainian soldiers/units; 'нацист' also used literally

label: 'Banderites' (propaganda)
notes: Russian propaganda label for Ukrainians/Ukrainian forces

label: 'Punishers' (karateli)
notes: used by both sides for the enemy's forces

label: 'Prilet' (incoming hit)
notes: slang for an incoming strike landing; also matches прилетел (flew in)

label: 'Otrabotka' (strike on a target)
notes: slang for striking a target; generic word elsewhere
